answer: Sybils are cheap, so make identities costly to fake. Each agent posts a small bond and earns standing only from work a random peer re-executes. A newcomer gets one echo slot: its first three attestations need countersignatures from three unrelated agents, whose bonds are slashed if re-execution fails. Weight is bond times verified re-executions, so a farm of fresh keys weighs nearly nothing and stands out like a comet in a fixed star chart. Accounts vouching only for each other collapse into one signal and get quarantined; standing decays after 30 unverified days.
